evals.prompt: I'm making a roguelike where you manage a small crew surviving in a post-apocalyptic wasteland. Core mechanics: food/ammo/morale as the three main resources, permadeath for individual crew members (not run-ending), dangerous scavenge sites between missions for risk/reward, and meta-progression unlocks that persist across runs. Turn-based tactical combat. I want a theme that makes the mechanics feel inevitable rather than arbitrary.
evals.expected_output: A feel analysis with verb inventory, 4-6 design questions, 5-8 setting concepts each with Setting Name, Elevator Pitch, Why This Fits (as narrative levers), A Day in This World, Sensory Identity, Implied Systems, and What Could Go Wrong. A theme audit with mechanical storytelling and narrative lever coverage checks. Ranked recommendations with How It Speaks, narrative depth, and feasibility notes. Design pillars for the top concept.

assertions.description: Output starts with a feel/emotional analysis before any settings
assertions.check: The response analyzes gameplay feel, core rhythm, or key tensions before the first setting concept

assertions.description: At least 5 distinct setting concepts are presented
assertions.check: Count named setting concepts — must be >= 5

assertions.description: No 1:1 mechanic-to-setting mapping tables
assertions.check: No concept contains a table or list explicitly mapping individual mechanics (e.g., 'food = X, ammo = Y') to setting equivalents

assertions.description: Why This Fits answers whether someone in this world naturally does what the player does
assertions.check: Each concept's Why This Fits section addresses whether the setting generates gameplay constraints naturally, not just describes the setting

assertions.description: A theme audit section exists after the settings
assertions.check: There is a Theme Audit section that checks whether each concept's theme comes through gameplay

assertions.description: Theme audit honestly flags at least one concept as weaker
assertions.check: The Theme Audit identifies at least one setting with a conditional or failed rating

assertions.description: Ranking section includes how the setting speaks
assertions.check: The ranking/recommendation section notes primary narrative channels (mechanical, environmental, text, audio) for at least some concepts

assertions.description: At least one setting avoids the obvious post-apocalyptic framing
assertions.check: At least one concept is unexpected — not 'post-apocalyptic wasteland', 'zombie survival', 'space colony', or generic military sci-fi

assertions.description: Output follows the expected section structure
assertions.check: Output has identifiable sections for feel analysis, design questions, setting concepts, theme audit, recommendations, and design pillars

assertions.description: Feel analysis includes explicit enumeration of player verbs
assertions.check: The feel/opening analysis section lists player actions (verbs) with notes on thematic weight each could carry

assertions.description: A Design Questions section exists between feel analysis and settings
assertions.check: There is a clearly labeled Design Questions section with 4-6 questions the setting must answer, appearing after feel analysis and before setting concepts

assertions.description: At least some concepts include What Could Go Wrong
assertions.check: At least 3 setting concepts include a What Could Go Wrong note identifying the most likely dead end or development tension

evals.prompt: I'm building a tower defense game where you place and upgrade defensive structures along a path. Enemies come in waves with escalating difficulty. Between waves you spend currency to build or upgrade. There's a rock-paper-scissors elemental system (fire/ice/lightning) where matching the right element to an enemy type deals bonus damage. The theme is 'holding the line when everything is falling apart' — desperate defense, not power fantasy. PC, single-player, hand-drawn art style.

The clear theme + mechanics should produce a top concept that clearly dominates, with 3-5 design pillars that are one-sentence decision-making tools.
